newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: FOCUS-Serbia PTT sells 49 pct telecom stake.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Serbia PTT sells 49 pct telecom stake.

text.p: Serbian Post and Communications (PTT) on Monday sold a 49 precent stake in its telecommunications department to Stet of Italy and OTE of Greece in a deal worth close to $1 billion, a senior Serbian official said on Monday.
"The deal was signed as we planned. We got 1.568 billion German marks for 49 percent stake of Serbian telecom," Dragan Peric, Serbian PTT's deputy general manager told Reuters.
Peric said Stet has bought 29 percent and OTE 20 percent of the Serbian Telecom in what he described as a "partnership deal".
"This is not a concession," a government official said.

"Negotiations were concluded sucessfully. We are very satisfied because the deal is positive for for further expansion of Stet activity in central and eastern Europe," said Tomaso Tommasi, Stet's managing director.
In Rome, Stet said it would pay 893 million German marks for its 29 stake with OTE paying 675 million marks.
It was the first major privatisation deal by Serbia, rushed through last month under a special law dividing Serbia's most valuable asset into postal services and telecommunications sector.
The law enabled the government to establish a separate telecommunications company Serbija Telekom prior to the sale to Stet and OTE.
Foreign partners would pay 80 percent of the sum immediately and the remaining sum in the first days of 1998, Serbia's minister for privatisation Milan Beko said.
The deal was scheduled for Sunday afternoon but was postponed to finalise "some technicalities," a source close to the Serbian negotiating team said on Sunday.
